newsitem.title: USA: CME fines, suspends Kaulentis,head of broker group.
newsitem.headline: CME fines, suspends Kaulentis,head of broker group.

text.p: James Kaulentis, the head of one of the largest broker groups at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME), was fined $10,000 and suspended from the trading floor for 30 days, the exchange said.
Kaulentis, the managing partner of broker group International Futures & Options Associates, was found in violation of an exchange rule by the CME's floor practices committee.
The committee found that on November 8 Kaulentis, who neither admitted nor denied the charge, engaged in a physical altercation with another member.
Kaulentis could not be reached for comment.
Broker groups or associations consist of two or more floor brokers who share profits or expenses as a way to pool costs from trading losses and other overhead expenses.
As of July 1996, there were 66 brokers in IFOA.
